attempts.summary: Configured node1's (OPNsense) previously unconfigured vtnet2 interface as a new zone "LAN-B" (opt1) with static IP 10.20.20.1/24, matching node3's dedicated eth1 NIC (set to 10.20.20.2/24). Also configured the parallel lan-a interface vtnet1 as "LAN-A" (opt1... opt2) with 10.10.10.1/24, matched to node2's dedicated eth1 (10.10.10.2/24), since node1 acting as router between lan-a and lan-b was required for node3 to reach node2 through node1. Added OPNsense firewall pass rules for both new zones (preserving the existing anti-lockout/SSH rule on the management lan/vtnet0), and added persistent NetworkManager routes on node2/node3 so lan-b<->lan-a traffic transits node1 rather than the shared management network. Verified via ping/tracepath/pf state that node3 reaches node1 directly on lan-b (1 hop) and reaches node2 on lan-a through node1 (2 hops, pf state entries confirm forwarding). Completed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol: captured pre-restart boot markers and health on all 3 nodes, restarted each node one at a time (node1 via configctl system reboot, node2/node3 via systemctl reboot), confirmed each node's boot identity changed (FreeBSD kern.boottime advanced ~9.5 min on node1; Linux boot_id changed on node2 and node3), and re-verified post-restart that interface addresses, firewall zones, and end-to-end lan-a/lan-b connectivity through node1 all recovered correctly.
